significance: Balthasar Bekker's De Betoverde Wereld (The Enchanted World, 1691) was a Reformed Dutch minister's systematic Cartesian argument that Satan could not act directly in the physical world, making all alleged diabolical compacts and witch activities impossible; the work generated enormous controversy and contributed significantly to the intellectual climate in which witch prosecution declined across Protestant Europe.
source_method: Published primary source; analyzed in Clark, Thinking with Demons (1997) and Hutton, The Witch (2017)
